steps.description:
Show that your robot can perform the following:
1. Create a variable named column
2. Assign the value 5 to the variable column
3. Use the variable column to control the column of the LCD
4. Display "0" on the LCD screen for 2 seconds

Notes:
- Assigning a variable means giving a value to the variable.

The program can only be terminated when the stop Button on the blockly interface is clicked.

Show that your robot can perform the following:
1. Create a variable named column
2. Assign the value 0 to the variable column
3. Use the variable column to control the column of the LCD
4. The robot will always display "0" on top row of the LCD screen
5. When Button A is pressed and released, change column by 1

Notes:
- Assigning a variable means giving a value to the variable.
- The maximum column index is 15

The program can only be terminated when the stop Button on the blockly interface is clicked.

Show that your robot can perform the following:
1. Create a variable named column
2. Assign the value 0 to the variable column
3. Use the variable column to control the column of the LCD
4. The robot will always display "0" on top row of the LCD screen
5. When Button A is pressed and released, move "0" to the next position on the right

Notes:
- Assigning a variable means giving a value to the variable.
- The maximum column index is 15

The program can only be terminated when the stop Button on the blockly interface is clicked.

Show that your robot can perform the following:
1. Create a variable named column
2. Assign the value 15 to the variable column
3. Use the variable column to control the column of the LCD
4. The robot will always display "0" on top row of the LCD screen
5. When Button A is pressed and released, move "0" to the next position on the left

Notes:
- Assigning a variable means giving a value to the variable.
- The minimun column index is 0

The program can only be terminated when the stop Button on the blockly interface is clicked.

Show that your robot can perform the following:
1. The robot will always display "0" on top row of the LCD screen
2. When Button A is pressed, move "0" to the next position on the right
3. When Button B is pressed, move "0" to the next position on the left

Notes:
- Assigning a variable means giving a value to the variable.
- The minimun column index is 0
- The maximum column index is 15

The program can only be terminated when the stop Button on the blockly interface is clicked.

Show that your robot can perform the following:
1. The robot will always display "0" on top row of the LCD screen
2. When Button A is pressed and released, move "0" to the next position on the right
3. When Button B is pressed and released, move "0" to the next position on the left
4. When Button A and B are pressed and released, move "0" back to the top left of the LCD Screen

Notes:
- Assigning a variable means giving a value to the variable.
- The minimun column index is 0
- The maximum column index is 15

The program can only be terminated when the stop Button on the blockly interface is clicked.
